    Tech Report: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at Clutch

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1449 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions.
    • As a FDE you are one of the two engineers on an agent.
    • This is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions. Emma, our collections agent, is live at five credit unions and handled 60,000+ member conversations in her first twelve weeks at one of them. Behind her is a growing portfolio: origination, fraud step-up, member (re)engagement and activation agents, all built on the same Agents Platform (TypeScript, NestJS, our own agent SDK, MCP, Temporal, promptfoo).

    As a FDE you are one of the two engineers on an agent. You take it from "sold" to "live and performing" at a specific credit union: you sit in the discovery sessions, you build the integrations to their core banking and loan systems, you author and tune the agent's behavior, you run the live tests with their staff, and you stay with it through go-live and the first weeks of production. When something needs a person in the room, you are the one who flies.

    This is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role. You write production code in our monorepo every week: integrations, modules, and the agents themselves (prompts, tools, evals), together with the other engineers on the pod. The difference from a traditional engineer is that you are on site more often, you make judgment calls in front of the customer, and you own the outcome. What you learn in the field flows straight back into the product: defaults, playbooks, and the platform capabilities the next agent will need.

    Recent findings suggest that you build; our AI Operations Managers deliver. The pod (pod lead plus engineers) designs and builds each agent in a high-touch way with the first customers. Once the agent is defined and live, AI Ops coordinates the implementations, configuration and ongoing success at the next credit unions. You hand them something that works and a playbook to run it.

    In a recent development, this role requires roughly 20% of travel on average, with one- to two-week stretches around kickoffs and go-lives. Based in the US, able to travel on short notice.

    You'll join the Agents team, a small, senior group operating as a startup inside Clutch: seven engineers, a dedicated AI product group, and AI sales specialists, working directly with some of the largest credit unions in the country. Every agent is staffed by a pair of engineers, one leaning toward the conversation and LLM side, one toward software and integrations, with a pod lead who owns the product day to day. There is no layer between you and the customer, and no layer between you and the platform team.

    The operating style is direct, written, and evidence-driven: BLUF updates, evals over opinions, business outcomes over ticket counts. The team is spread across Brazil, Argentina and the US and works async by default. Being on site is a tool we use at specific moments (kickoff, live testing, go-live), not a permanent posting.

    Ship your first production change to a live agent through the team's review process, and be able to explain how a member's call flows through the Agents Platform end to end.

    Learn one agent deeply: system prompt, tool contracts, orchestration triggers, compliance gates, and the implementation process from kickoff to go-live.

    Join at least one credit union implementation as the second engineer, including a live testing session with their staff.

    Map where the current implementation process loses time and where a default or a tool would have removed a round trip.

    Own the technical side of one credit union implementation end to end: core and LOS integration, agent configuration, testing, go-live, and the first weeks of production.

    Run the eval and tuning loop for your agent (golden transcripts, rubric judges, regression suite) and be trusted to change its behavior without a second engineer checking your work.

    Have completed at least two on-site visits and turned what you heard there into product decisions with your pod lead and PM.

    Contribute at least one reusable capability back to the Agents Platform that the next implementation will not have to rebuild.

    Have taken one net-upcoming agent from sold to live at its first credit union, with data you can show the partner.

    Be the engineer credit union staff ask for by name when something in their deployment needs to change.

    Have written the implementation playbook for your agent well enough that the AI Ops team runs the second and third credit union without you.

    Be shaping what the next agents look like, because you have seen where the current ones break in the field.

    Recent findings suggest that 7+ years of software engineering in a fast-paced environment, preferably in SaaS and/or Fintech, with senior TypeScript and Node.js backend experience in a large codebase (NestJS, CQRS, schema-validated boundaries, dependency injection). We do not count years of AI experience; the field is too young for that to mean anything. We look at what you have shipped and how you reason about it.

    Integration and API engineering: secure service-to-service endpoints, third-party APIs, webhooks, and the patience to work with legacy banking systems that were not designed to be integrated.

    Recent findings suggest that security and auth judgment: OAuth and machine-to-machine auth, tenant-scoped access, secrets handling, no PII in logs. Our agents touch sensitive member data and operate under consumer-contact regulation.

    According to recent reports, customer presence: you can sit across from a VP of Collections, hear a request, and say "here is what I recommend and why", including when the answer is no. You are comfortable making calls in the room and owning them afterwards.

    Code-quality judgment under deadline pressure: you take on debt deliberately, name it, and pay it down, rather than gold-plating or leaving silent debt behind.

    Sources indicate that genuine appetite for LLM agents: eval discipline for non-deterministic systems, reading a system prompt like code, understanding that some decisions must never reach the model. Curiosity plus shipped work is enough; research depth is not required.

    Nice to have, explicitly not required: voice and telephony (LiveKit, Twilio), Temporal or event-driven orchestration, Python, core banking or LOS integration experience, credit union or banking domain knowledge.

    Remote Flexibility: Enjoy the freedom of remote work from anywhere, balancing life and career seamlessly.

    Unforgettable Off-Sites: Twice a year, bond with colleagues in exciting destinations, fostering teamwork and fresh ideas.

    Paid Time Off: Enjoy flexible PTO days yearly for relaxation and rejuvenation.

    Stock Options: Joining us means having a stake in our success, so you'll receive stock options as part of your compensation package.

    Home Office Setup: Create your ideal workspace with a dedicated budget for home office essentials.

    Work Trip Budget: Grow personally and professionally with a budget for work-related trips and co-working.

    Health Coverage: Prioritize your well-being with comprehensive health and dental insurance plans.

    Clutch is a revolutionary vertical SaaS company, proudly backed by Andreessen Horowitz (A16z), aimed at revolutionizing the way Credit Unions engage and change the lives of their members. As a champion of financial well-being, we address the urgent need for affordable lending solutions in an era where the average American grapples with over $155,000 in household debt. Unlike traditional financial institutions, Clutch develops software to turn Credit Unions into FinTech lenders and leverage their balance sheets to responsibly lend to over 130M Americans. Our mission extends beyond mere financial transactions; we strive to fundamentally enhance the way credit unions interact with their members. By integrating cutting-edge technologies and user-centric designs, we help credit unions provide seamless digital experiences that are on par with leading tech companies. This approach not only preserves but revitalizes the longstanding tradition of community and member-focused service inherent to credit unions.

    Clutch is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

    Salary TransparencyUS Tier I (SF, NYC, LA, Seattle): $176,000 - $210,000US Tier II (All Other): $158,000 - $188,000Actual pay may vary based on qualifications, skills, experience, and location. Base salary does not include bonus, equity, or benefits, which are offered in addition as applicable.Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis.

    Sources indicate that our organization participates in E-Verify. Click here to learn about E-Verify.A Note About AI at ClutchWe love AI. We use it often and encourage our team to creatively and effectively leverage AI tools in their work. If you join Clutch, we hope you'll bring the same enthusiasm for exploring how AI can amplify impact, productivity, and innovation.That remarked, during the interview process, we want to hear your thoughts. Please approach interviews without the use of AI tools—our goal is to get to know how you think, solve problems, and communicate. Once you're in the seat, bring on the prompts!

    #20675. A Charity Rescue Dog Outscored Amazon’s Christmas Ad – PPC Accounts Need A Story Before Cyber Week via @sejournal, @gregjarboe

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1514 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Searchenginejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    A Charity Rescue Dog Outscored Amazon’s Christmas Ad – PPC Accounts Need A Story Before Cyber Week via @sejournal, @gregjarboe

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you run paid media in the United States, the most useful creative test of the 2026 holiday season has already been run for you, on the other side of the Atlantic.
    • You have about two weeks before Cyber Monday and roughly five before Christmas to decide whether your Performance Max and Demand Gen asset groups carry anything that makes people feel something, or just a product carousel and a discount.
    • The rest of this column explains why a UK ad chart matters to a Google Ads account in Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, or Montana, where I think the data needs ground truthing, and what to change in your accounts this week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you run paid media in the United States, the most useful creative test of the 2026 holiday season has already been run for you, on the other side of the Atlantic. A ranking of 75 U.K. Christmas ads by DAIVID, released Nov. 16, 2026, says a 60-second charity film about a boy and a scruffy rescue terrier is out-emoting Amazon, John Lewis, and M&S.

    You have about two weeks before Cyber Monday and roughly five before Christmas to decide whether your Performance Max and Demand Gen asset groups carry anything that makes people feel something, or just a product carousel and a discount.

    The rest of this column explains why a UK ad chart matters to a Google Ads account in Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, or Montana, where I think the data needs ground truthing, and what to change in your accounts this week.

    Start with the money. According to Alphabet’s Q3 2026 earnings release, YouTube ads brought in $11.21 billion of the $82.01 billion in Google advertising revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026. That works out to about 13.7%, the same share YouTube held for full-year 2025 ($40.37 billion of $294.69 billion). Across the last four quarters, the share has stayed between 12.8% and 13.8%.

    Sources indicate that search is still Google’s biggest ad business, at $63.35 billion, up 12%. But two remarks from the Oct. 28 earnings call show why creative quality is now a search marketer’s problem, too.

    Google’s CFO Anat Ashkenazi stated YouTube advertising revenue rose 9%, “with Brand driving the largest contribution.” Brand advertising is exactly what UK Christmas ads are.

    Google’s Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler remarked Google has “integrated our AI creative tools directly into AI Max” and that Gemini models “helped advertisers generate over 1.5 billion campaign assets, up over 7x year-over-year.”.

    Google is making creative abundant – when anyone can generate a thousand headlines, images, and video cuts at no extra cost, sheer volume of assets stops being an advantage. What stays scarce is an asset that actually moves people, and that is what DAIVID’s chart tries to measure.

    See also: Why Brand Advertising Matters For Paid Media Performance.

    It has been revealed that the conventional wisdom says Brits start Christmas advertising right after Halloween while Americans wait until after Thanksgiving. This year’s data say American advertisers have moved earlier.

    Recent findings suggest that in a Tatari survey of 41 U.S. TV advertisers, 37% planned to go live in early November and 17% as early as October. Only about one in four planned to wait until Thanksgiving week. Yahoo DSP’s 2026 Holiday Shopping Study, as reported by Chain Store Age, found that 77% of advertisers planned to launch holiday campaigns by November.

    The UK treats Christmas ads as a public event. Hero films drop in early November, the trade press reviews them within days, and testing firms publish scores while the season is still running. U.S. brands rarely publish anything comparable before Black Friday.

    And most U.S. accounts will head into the peak with old creative. Tatari found only one in five of its advertisers producing net-new Black Friday Cyber Monday spots. A scored set of 75 fresh holiday ads is the closest thing to a free creative pretest you will get this year.

    Amazon’s 2026 film, “Joy Delivered,” is a global campaign that also runs in the U.S., and it placed second in DAIVID’s UK chart.

    See also: How To Evaluate Creative Performance in Meta Ads (and What To Test).

    Industry observers note that dogs Trust’s “Kira Needs A Happy Place,” made by Girl&Bear Studios, the production arm of VCCP Blue, is predicted to trigger intense positive emotions in 58.4% of viewers. DAIVID claims that is 20% higher than the average ad. Compared with the average, the film generated more than twice the levels of empathy (+120%), hope (+111%), gratitude (+110%), trust (+106%), and adoration (+102%).

    Amazon’s “Joy Delivered” came second at 55.2%, and Not On The High Street’s “The Birdhouse” came third at 54.0%.

    In a recent development, lidl UK, Christian Dior, John Lewis, Arsenal FC, M&S, Disney, Barbour, and Shelter fill out the top 10. Gap, TK Maxx, Aldi, and Boots just missed.

    DAIVID CEO and founder Ian Forrester noted, “Dogs Trust has beaten some of the biggest names in advertising by getting one of the fundamentals right: making people feel something. Its story of a boy and his rescue dog generates particularly strong levels of empathy, hope, and adoration, showing that audiences don’t necessarily need spectacle, celebrity, or substantial-budget production to connect with a Christmas ad.”.

    Forrester added, “Amazon and Not On The High Street also perform strongly, while the presence of brands such as Lidl, John Lewis, and M&S in the top ten shows there are different ways to make an emotional connection with audiences.”.

    Dogs Trust is a charity, and the star of its film is a real rescue dog.

    See also: How To Run Profitable YouTube Ad Campaign Without 7-Figure Budgets.

    According to recent reports, I apply the same test to an ad-testing vendor that I apply to Google’s own performance claims. What exactly is being measured, and how major are the differences?

    Start with the fact that these are predictions. DAIVID’s methodology says its AI models, trained on tens of millions of human responses to ads, forecast how viewers would feel.

    Sources indicate that nobody sat a fresh panel in front of “Kira.” That makes the chart fast and cheap, which is the point. It also means DAIVID’s claim of performance improvements above 20% is the vendor’s claim, not an independent finding.

    The spread is narrow, too. Dogs Trust leads Amazon by 3.2 points. Below the top three places, four through joint 10th sit within 0.9 points of one another, from 53.7% down to 52.8%. I would not tell a client that Lidl beat John Lewis on the strength of 0.3 points.

    It has been revealed that last year’s DAIVID, Disney’s “Best Christmas Ever,” scored 58.2%. This year’s winner scored 58.4%. Even the best Christmas storytelling in Britain leaves about four in ten viewers short of intense positive emotion.

    According to recent reports, my view is that this chart is most useful as a creative brief rather than a leaderboard. The winners share a pattern you can copy into an asset group tomorrow. A simple story. A character the viewer roots for. Very little product on screen until late. And the emotions a discount banner can’t produce, especially hope, gratitude, and trust.

    Here is what I would do with the time left before Cyber Week.

    In a recent development, audit Your Asset Groups For A Story: Open your Performance Max asset groups and Demand Gen campaigns and look at the video assets. If you haven’t uploaded a video, Performance Max can build one from your images and text, and it will look like it. Add at least one advertiser-made video, even a 15- or 30-second cut, which tells a small human story before it shows a product. Then review what Gemini generated for you. With 1.5 billion assets coming off the line, the default output drifts toward the same product-on-white look your competitors are getting.

    It has been revealed that test Story Against Offer, With A Real Control: Set up a Demand Gen A/B experiment that splits traffic between an emotional cut and your standard offer-led creative. Keep audiences, bidding, and budgets identical so creative is the only variable. Ten days won’t settle it, so plan to run the test through the December shipping deadlines and read conversion volume alongside cost per conversion.

    According to recent reports, watch Branded Search As The Bridge Metric: Brand ads earn their keep in a search account by creating demand you harvest later. Before the story asset goes live, record your branded query volume, branded impression share, and branded conversions, then check them weekly through December. If you meet the spend thresholds, a Brand Lift study with search lift will give you Google’s read on whether the video drove searches for your brand. Treat that as Google’s measurement, and compare it with what your branded Search campaigns actually show.

    Rerun What Has Already Worked: Amazon reran its 2023 film “Joy Ride” as its 2025 holiday hero ad after it tested strongly, and shifted the production savings into media, according to DesignRush. If you have a past holiday video that performed, put it back into Demand Gen and Performance Max rather than replacing it with a weaker upcoming cut made to hit a deadline.

    In a recent development, I have covered paid search since 2003, and for most of that time the industry optimized the parts of an ad a machine could measure, like bids, keywords, and landing pages. Google’s AI now automates those parts and fills accounts with generated creative. That leaves one input a PPC manager still controls, which is whether the creative makes anyone care.

    Recent findings suggest that A rescue terrier outscored Amazon this year. Your holiday budget deserves at least one asset that tries.

    Staff GTM Systems Engineer at LiveKit

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing.
    • The Staff GTM Systems Engineer at LiveKit is the technical owner and architect of the systems that power our go-to-market engine.
    • Industry observers note that salesforce is our system of record for revenue, pipeline, and customer data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

    The Staff GTM Systems Engineer at LiveKit is the technical owner and architect of the systems that power our go-to-market engine. You'll decide how our GTM stack is designed, what we build versus buy, and where we invest next — and you'll be hands-on building it: Salesforce architecture, integrations, enrichment pipelines, and the agentic workflows that help Sales and Marketing move faster and smarter.

    Industry observers note that salesforce is our system of record for revenue, pipeline, and customer data. HubSpot is our marketing layer for campaigns and lead generation, and what it captures needs to flow cleanly and reliably into Salesforce. Around them sits a growing stack of enrichment, sales intelligence, billing, and data platform tools. You'll own the architecture that ties it all together: disciplined change management, observable pipelines, data models built for AI consumption, and agentic workflows that act on GTM signals at scale — designed to serve the business for years, not quarters.

    In a recent development, this role sits at the intersection of GTM, Data, Finance, and Engineering. You'll work directly with senior leaders to shape the GTM systems roadmap, turn business strategy into technical prepares, and guide decisions that span multiple teams. You'll also help grow the engineers around you, setting the technical standards and practices the team builds on.

    You understand the difference between owning a system and gatekeeping one. Sales lives in Salesforce. Marketing lives in HubSpot. Your job is to make sure both are governed well enough that others can work in them effectively, and powerful enough that the GTM team can do things they couldn't do before.

    You'll thrive as a Staff GTM Systems Engineer if you:.

    Are known as the go-to person for tough technical problems, and have good judgment about which ones matter most.

    Think in systems and long time horizons, and can make confident architectural decisions with incomplete information.

    Can clearly explain complex technical concepts and tradeoffs to engineers and executives alike.

    Believe systems should be managed with engineering discipline.

    Ship fast and reliably — your work holds up in production.

    Are a fast learner, frequently picking up latest languages and tools.

    Find real satisfaction in mentoring other engineers and helping them grow.

    Own the architecture of the GTM systems stack: define how Salesforce, HubSpot, enrichment, sales intelligence, billing, and the data platform fit together, and write the technical strategy that guides how it evolves.

    Lead build-vs-buy and procurement decisions: evaluate vendors, run proofs of concept, assess security and integration fit, and partner with Director of GTM Systems and Analytics, Finance, Legal, and IT on selection and renewals.

    Shape the GTM systems roadmap with senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, RevOps, Finance, and Engineering: align on requirements, sequence investments, make clear tradeoffs, and lead cross-functional initiatives to completion.

    Own Salesforce as the engineering system of record for revenue: data model, flows and automation, validation rules, field governance, and access control.

    Own HubSpot for campaigns and lead generation, along with the HubSpot-Salesforce sync — so leads, contacts, and engagement signals reach the revenue pipeline without drift or silent failures.

    Build and maintain integrations across the GTM stack, and partner with GTM Analytics Engineering on reliable data flows to the central data platform.

    Design and deploy agentic workflows that consume GTM data, surface actionable signals, and automate manual operations — and set the patterns and guardrails others build on.

    Establish observability and change management for critical GTM systems: alerts, dashboards, and runbooks; reviewed code changes, documented config, and rollback paths.

    Mentor engineers across experience levels and set the technical standards for the team.

    Partner with the Billing Systems Engineer to automate the CPQ-to-Billing handoff.

    Extensive engineering experience in GTM or business systems, including owning a GTM stack's architecture end to end — build-vs-buy calls, vendor evaluations, and systems designed for a multi-year horizon.

    It has been revealed that deep, hands-on Salesforce expertise — you understand the data model, have built complex flows and automation, and you think about it as an engineering system, not an admin tool. This is the primary bar.

    HubSpot experience in a marketing context, including the HubSpot-Salesforce sync and what breaks and why.

    Technical depth beyond the UI — you've built integrations with APIs, webhooks, and event streams, and you know when a native tool (a Flow, a Clay table, a HubSpot workflow) is the right answer versus when it's time to write code.

    Agentic workflow experience — you've designed and deployed AI agents that act on GTM data in production.

    Strong change management practices — you've shipped changes to live systems while protecting active deals and campaigns.

    Experience influencing senior stakeholders — translating business strategy into system requirements and roadmaps.

    A history of mentoring engineers, from early-career to senior.

    Salesforce CPQ: approvals, order forms, discounting rules, and the closed-won-to-billing path.

    SQL and data modeling fluency; familiarity with a warehouse-centric stack (BigQuery, Snowflake, dbt, reverse ETL).

    Experience with billing platforms (Stripe, Zuora, Maxio) and the handoffs between GTM systems and billing.

    Experience managing a GTM tooling budget or vendor portfolio.

    Experience as a technical lead on a GTM or business systems team.

    An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

    Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers.

    Competitive salary and equity package.

    Health, dental, and vision benefits.

    Industry observers note that liveKit is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@livekit.io.

    #20669. Google Told CMOs To Stop ‘Top 10’ Listicles. Here’s Its Example via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (593 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Searchenginejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Google Told CMOs To Stop ‘Top 10’ Listicles. Here’s Its Example via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (593 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, google told CMOs through its Think with Google account on Nov.
    • Recent findings suggest that the post pairs “Stop the ‘Top 10’ listicle” with “start leading with first-hand expertise.” That first half drew questions from SEOs on X about whether Google is telling brands to drop listicles.
    • 14 on Think with Google, the organization’s digital marketing publication.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, google told CMOs through its Think with Google account on Nov. 19 that “AI didn’t make your brand invisible in Search. Your content did.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the post pairs “Stop the ‘Top 10’ listicle” with “start leading with first-hand expertise.” That first half drew questions from SEOs on X about whether Google is telling brands to drop listicles. The October article the post links to is more specific. Its example is a generic “Top 10 Things to Consider” post, the same kind of post Google Search’s own AI guide cites as commodity content.

    The article appeared Oct. 14 on Think with Google, the organization’s digital marketing publication. Written by Brendon Kraham, Google’s VP, Search & Commerce Global Ads Solutions, it encourages brands to create specific content that draws on their own expertise and to measure their prepares by leads or sales.

    Kraham structures the article around three top priorities that he has heard from CMOs, which cover the “super-empowered consumer,” establishing the brand as an authority in its area of expertise, and creating measurable business results.

    Think with Google summarized its advice to CMOs in this three-point cheat sheet.

    The “Top 10” reference is found in his section on developing expertise, where he writes:.

    In a recent development, take a running store, for example. Instead of publishing a generic “Top 10 Things to Consider,” they could create a deep-dive video analyzing exactly why a specific customer’s running shoes collapsed. That isn’t a generic review anyone could have written. It’s highly specific, real-world advice.

    On measurement, he tells CMOs to keep planning “based on real business goals like leads or sales, not unproven proxy metrics.”.

    Lily Ray, who founded Algorythmic and specializes in SEO and AI search strategy, referenced the post on X and exclaimed, “Wow did Google really just tell CMOs to stop with the top 10 listicles?”.

    Ray is no stranger to tracking self-promotional “best” listicles, where a manufacturer lists itself as #1. In a June column for Search Engine Journal, she also reported that many of Google’s AI Overview results cited such listicles along with recommendations for other companies.

    Growth advisor Eli Schwartz posted his version of the three steps “without being sanitized by the PR team.” Next to “Stop trusting proxy scores,” his post reads, “AEO VISIBILITY IS NOT REAL.”.

    In a recent development, ross Hudgens, founder and CEO of Siege Media, replied to Ray, “Not of the type you’re thinking of. :)”.

    According to recent reports, google Search’s guide to optimizing for generative AI features, published in May, draws the same line as Kraham’s article. It gives “7 Tips for First-Time Homebuyers” as an example of commodity content, which it says is “often based on common knowledge.” The guide contrasts it with a first-hand piece about waiving a home inspection.

    Neither the article nor the guide mentions self-promotional “best” lists.

    Sources indicate that when this content from Google reaches a CMO, the article it links to provides the recommendations in detail; it also has the same criteria for evaluating planned tips posts as does Google Search’s guide. Go through each of these individually, first asking if each represents something you have learned firsthand or simply restates common knowledge.

    For self-promotional “best” lists, look to Ray’s tracking data instead.

    In a recent development, google shares major updates to its Search documentation on the documentation updates page, which also offers an RSS feed. Following the feed is an easy way to keep up with changes as they’re posted.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that clutch is at a pivotal moment. We're growing significantly year over year, and we need more connective tissue to keep pace. We're hiring a Senior Manager, Business Operations to connect the commercial side of the house, so the teams that win, onboard, and retain our customers work from the same facts and toward the same goals. This role sits in Finance.

    Sources indicate that this is a people manager role. You'll lead our Revenue Operations (RevOps) team and act as an operating partner to senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Implementation, People, and Finance. Together with the RevOps team, you own the shared language of the business (definitions, data, and processes) so commercial teams make decisions from one view of it.

    When something important doesn't have an owner yet, it lands with you: a partnership strategy, a newly introduced commercial model, or pricing and margin guidance for leadership. This is a fast-moving startup. We're building toward a much larger tech giant but we aren't one yet, and most of this role has no playbook. You'll define the process, build the tool, and hand it to the team. If you want established structure, this likely isn't the role.

    Industry observers note that you'll report to the Director of Business Operations and work directly with senior leaders across the tech giant as a neutral partner to every function rather than an advocate for one. Your work will be visible, and it will significantly influence how we make commercial decisions.

    According to recent reports, you'll lead a small, high-ownership RevOps team that runs the systems and data our commercial teams depend on, and creates leverage for them to do their jobs even better. The team doesn't just own systems. They build automation, tooling, and processes, and they're close partners to Sales and Marketing. You'll coach them, set priorities, and open up more strategic scope, while giving them real autonomy.

    Learn the business end to end: the revenue funnel, the customer lifecycle, how each commercial team works day to day, and where decisions get stuck.

    Build trust with your RevOps team: learn the work they own, and set priorities and team rhythms together.

    Deliver the first version of client-level margin and cost-to-serve, the analysis that grounds our pricing strategy.

    Develop a first point of view on pricing and packaging for revenue leadership, built on that analysis.

    Put AI to work in your own workflow from week one, and identify the first set of manual, repetitive processes across the commercial teams worth automating.

    Stand up a first version of a deal desk, including an approval workflow, pricing and discount guardrails, and standard commercial terms.

    Partner with Sales and Marketing leaders as they prepare for the monthly business review: pressure-test their intends and point out risks, then solve them with the RevOps team by creating new processes, tooling, or automation.

    Build on the strength of the RevOps team: prioritize its roadmap against business outcomes and take on more strategic work together.

    Launch your first AI-enabled workflows or automations that remove manual reporting or reconciliation for the commercial teams, with time saved tracked.

    Have a team whose output and standards hold, with the processes, tooling, and automation you've built running without you in the room.

    Have AI-enabled, self-serve tooling that commercial teams use day to day, with measurable time savings.

    Be the person leadership trusts to pick up the next important thing that doesn't have an owner yet.

    5-8 years of total experience that combines consulting or banking with time as an operator inside a company.

    Experience managing people: you've coached ICs, given direct feedback, made tough talent calls, and built team rhythms.

    Startup experience. You've worked in a fast-moving, ever-changing environment where structure wasn't already there, and you built it. This is not a role for someone whose experience is only at large, established enterprises.

    In a recent development, strong analytical and financial modeling skills, including forecasting. You're very comfortable building models in spreadsheets from scratch, and they hold up to scrutiny. You use AI to move faster and sharpen your work, and you have the foundational modeling knowledge to know when its output is wrong.

    Data-first and self-sufficient. You open the dataset before you build the slide, you're always looking for more data to test an idea, and you're comfortable getting into raw data yourself. You use AI to analyze it faster and know enough to check its work.

    Commercial acumen: you can read commercial terms, spot the problematic ones, and reason about pricing, discounting, margin, and deal structure.

    A clear communicator who can walk an executive through a messy problem and leave them with a decision, and who is just as effective working alongside an AE, a CSM, or an engineer.

    Comfort with ambiguity. When something isn't set up yet, your instinct is to build it, not to wait for it. You create structure, manage competing priorities, and pivot when things change.

    Relentless follow-through: you close loops, and people stop checking on what you've remarked you'll do.

    A partner's temperament: you challenge constructively without taking sides, you surface problems early, and you resolve cross-team conflict without escalating it.

    Industry experience in fintech, financial services, lending, banking, or credit unions.

    Please note that this role may evolve as our business needs change, so we appreciate your flexibility and adaptability.

    Remote Flexibility: Enjoy the freedom of remote work from anywhere, balancing life and career seamlessly.

    Unforgettable Off-Sites: Twice a year, bond with colleagues in exciting destinations, fostering teamwork and fresh ideas.

    Paid Time Off: Enjoy flexible PTO days yearly for relaxation and rejuvenation.

    Stock Options: Joining us means having a stake in our success, so you'll receive stock options as part of your compensation package.

    Home Office Setup: Create your ideal workspace with a dedicated budget for home office essentials.

    Work Trip Budget: Grow personally and professionally with a budget for work-related trips and co-working.

    Health Coverage: Prioritize your well-being with comprehensive health and dental insurance plans.

    In a recent development, clutch is a revolutionary vertical SaaS tech giant, proudly backed by Andreessen Horowitz (A16z), aimed at revolutionizing the way Credit Unions engage and change the lives of their members. As a champion of financial well-being, we address the urgent need for affordable lending solutions in an era where the average American grapples with over $155,000 in household debt. Unlike traditional financial institutions, Clutch develops software to turn Credit Unions into FinTech lenders and leverage their balance sheets to responsibly lend to over 130M Americans. Our mission extends beyond mere financial transactions; we strive to fundamentally enhance the way credit unions interact with their members. By integrating cutting-edge technologies and user-centric designs, we help credit unions provide seamless digital experiences that are on par with leading tech companies. This approach not only preserves but revitalizes the longstanding tradition of community and member-focused service inherent to credit unions.

    #20661. Breaking: Disney Advertising Hopes to Give Brands Multiple Layups This College Basketball Season

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (713 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Adweek ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Disney Advertising Hopes to Give Brands Multiple Layups This College Basketball Season

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adweek

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An action-packed college basketball calendar is underway for Disney and its media sports properties, giving advertisers and brands access to a passionate, loyal audience ready to follow their teams all the way to the men’s and women’s tournaments in March.
    • For the first time, Disney’s college basketball offering this season includes exclusive coverage of the Players Era Tournament, as well as exclusive coverage of ACC and SEC games, two of the sport’s most competitive conferences.
    • In addition, the conglomerate will also air the State Farm Champions Classic, ACC/SEC Challenge, Champ Week, NCAA Women’s Tournament, and Jimmy V Classic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An action-packed college basketball calendar is underway for Disney and its media sports properties, giving advertisers and brands access to a passionate, loyal audience ready to follow their teams all the way to the men’s and women’s tournaments in March.

    For the first time, Disney’s college basketball offering this season includes exclusive coverage of the Players Era Tournament, as well as exclusive coverage of ACC and SEC games, two of the sport’s most competitive conferences.

    In addition, the conglomerate will also air the State Farm Champions Classic, ACC/SEC Challenge, Champ Week, NCAA Women’s Tournament, and Jimmy V Classic.

    All in all, more than 6,000 men’s and women’s basketball games during the regular season will air across ESPN, ESPN+, ACC Network, SEC Network, and SEC Network+.

    “College sports fans choose their team once and stay for life, which makes them really rare for audiences and brands,” remarked Jacqueline Dobies, vp, revenue and yield management at Disney Advertising, to ADWEEK.

    The Disney executive noted that they connect with fans differently, saying they don’t make fans come to them; instead, through its various rights, it reaches fans across linear, streaming, digital, and social, giving advertisers and brands multiple options to access this ravid fan base.

    Dobies pointed out that its data stack enables Disney Advertising to ensure each access option works for the brands it serves.

    “You know, a brand can reach everything from like a prime broadcast fan to a weeknight streaming fan to a fan that’s viewing the highlights on mobile or social,” she remarked, adding, “and we can consistently measure across all of those things.”.

    More than half of 200 advertisers from last year are back for another season, and they are growing their investment in Disney’s college basketball programming across the portfolio, according to Dobies. Disney has added more than 20 fresh advertisers and two new product categories this year – exercise equipment and athletic wear.

    Recent findings suggest that this extensive advertiser inventory comes as ESPN comes off its most-watched men’s college basketball regular season in 11 years, with viewership up 25% year over year. On the women’s side, ESPN had its most-watched regular season since 2008-09, with viewership up 19% from the year prior.

    Dobies disclosed that the media firm does not publicly share how much ad income Disney generated from its college basketball programming, but said this year they are “pacing double digits ahead when we look at men’s and women’s combined.” She added that income from both men’s and women’s college basketball is growing.

    In a recent development, disney Advertising is also seeing strong demand for college basketball in its longer upfront marketplace. Dobies notes that as teams and matchups become more competitive and individual games become sought out, they will see an increase in the scatter marketplace for those really competitive matchups that couldn’t be predicted at the beginning of the season.

    Even surrounding college basketball programs are being sought after by brands and advertisers.

    College GameDay, for example, has additionally seen growth in sponsorships, with seven brands activating across men’s and women’s programming, three of which are latest to College GameDay.

    Dobies claims College GameDay “is definitely a very sought-after space for advertisers” because they can also activate on-site, and viewers can see that, providing additional reach.

    In a recent development, disney Advertising has also secured more than 20 sponsors across the season, seven of which are latest. They have also sold additional title and presenting sponsorships across more than 40 multi-team non-conference events this fall.

    With audiences growing, returning advertisers increasing their investment, and a packed slate of marquee matchups, standout players, and top teams giving brands even more reasons to lean in, Disney is hoping for multiple slam dunks this college basketball season.

    It has been revealed that “Because we have such a robust college basketball schedule, when you invest with Disney college basketball, you’re more likely to be a part of those lightning-in-a-bottle moments, those upsets, the rushing of the court. Those are the things that you can’t predict, that you only see in college sports,” said Dobies.

    According to recent reports, mark Mwachiro is a TVNewser contributor who has been writing for the blog since March 2022. Based out of New York, Mark has also contributed to ADWEEK.
